questions.q: Support tickets arrive at an average of 4 per hour, independently. What distribution describes the time gap between consecutive tickets?
options: Uniform
Normal
Log-normal
Exponential
questions.explain: Events that follow a Poisson process have exponentially distributed gaps between them.

questions.q: What does 'memoryless' mean for an exponential waiting time?
options: The chance of waiting longer is unaffected by how long you have already waited
The distribution forgets its own mean
Older data points are given less weight
The variable can never be negative
questions.explain: For an exponential, P(X > a + b | X > a) equals P(X > b). It is an assumption that real systems often violate.

questions.q: A variable is strongly right-skewed with skewness 2.28, but np.log of it has skewness near 0. Which model fits the original variable best?
options: Uniform
Log-normal
Geometric
Student's t
questions.explain: If the log of a variable is approximately normal, the variable itself is log-normal.

questions.q: np.random.default_rng().lognormal(3.5, 0.6) takes 3.5 and 0.6 as which quantities?
options: The mean and sd of the resulting log-normal values
The mean and sd of the underlying normal on the log scale
The median and variance of the result
The minimum and maximum of the result
questions.explain: numpy's parameters describe the underlying normal distribution. The mean of the results is exp(mu + sigma^2/2), which is why the sample mean was about 40, not 3.5.

questions.q: For a 95% interval, the t critical value with df = 5 is 2.571 and with df = 1000 is 1.962. What does this show?
options: The t distribution has lighter tails than the normal
Degrees of freedom do not matter for inference
The t distribution needs a wider multiplier for small samples and converges to the normal as df grows
The t distribution only works with df above 1000
questions.explain: Small samples carry extra uncertainty, so t has heavier tails and a bigger multiplier; with large df it is nearly the normal value of 1.96.
